{{Quote|If this body is not capable of action, I suggest new leadership is needed.|[[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Queen Amidala]]|<ref name="Episode 1">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
The '''Supreme Chancellor election of [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]''' was the last time a new [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] was chosen. The election was held after Chancellor [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] lost a [[Vote of No Confidence/Legends|Vote of No Confidence]] in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] due to the Republic's mishandling of the crisis on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. Though [[Bail Antilles/Legends|Bail Antilles]] and [[Ainlee Teem/Legends|Ainlee Teem]] were nominated as Valorum's successor, the Senate voted overwhelmingly to support then-[[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] of Naboo, at the time a relatively obscure figure. Though outside observers considered Palpatine's election to be a surprise, he had manipulated events (both in his public identity and in his secret role as Darth Sidious, [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]]) to ensure not only that an early election would be held, but that he would win it. After winning the election, Palpatine led [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] as Chancellor and as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] for thirty-six years.

==Background==
{{Quote|Well, Magister Damask, of course. He controls all of it. Even the coming election on Coruscant.''"<br />"''Damask will put Senator Palpatine in power?''"<br />"''Naboo's favorite son? Hasn't Damask already done so?|[[Leika]] and [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] discuss Hego Damask|<ref name="End Game">{{StoryCite|story=End Game|book=Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|bformatted=''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization, 2012 edition}}</ref>}}
[[File:Valorum.jpg|thumb|left|Outgoing [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]]]]
Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum, a member of the [[Core Faction/Legends|Core faction]] of Senators, had been [[Supreme Chancellor election, 40 BBY|elected to his position]] in [[40 BBY/Legends|40 BBY]], and [[Supreme Chancellor election, 36 BBY/Legends|re-elected]] in [[36 BBY/Legends|36 BBY]], largely due to the influence and fame of [[House Valorum/Legends|his family]]. He was widely accepted to be an honorable man who truly desired the best for the galaxy; however, his stated position of continuing Republic policies detrimental to major corporations, slow responses to developing situations, reliance on bureaucracy, and conservative nature angered many in the opposing [[Rim Faction/Legends|Rim faction]] and even left many of his supporters doubtful of him. The rumor that Valorum was carrying out an affair with his [[Senior Administrative Aide/Legends|Senior Administrative Aide]], [[Sei Taria/Legends|Sei Taria]], no doubt also contributed to his plummeting support.

In [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], things finally came to a head. His role in the [[Yinchorri Uprising]] resulted in him ordering two [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] to their deaths, and in the resulting negotiations for a [[Yinchorri embargo act|blockade]] he had to use up his last political favors in convincing the Senate's core members to back his plan. The long delay before action was finally taken made him appear weak and caused his political career to dive in the eyes of the public.

A short while later, the [[Nebula Front/Legends|Nebula Front]] [[Dorvalla Incident|destroyed]] a [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|cargo ship]] over [[Dorvalla/Legends|Dorvalla]]. The Senators of the Rim faction demanded that the restrictions on the large corporations arming themselves be lifted; Senator Palpatine, one of Valorum's closest advisers, recommended that Valorum concede, but at the cost of taxing the free-trade zones that, ironically, had been established by Valorum's father. This caused an uproar when Valorum announced "his" plan to the Galactic Senate; however, the situation was somewhat ameliorated when Palpatine suggested to the Senate his plans for a [[Eriadu Trade Summit|trade summit]], to consist of representatives from the Senate, important commerce worlds, and the industrial groups.

The summit was set on the planet [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]], but was marked by disaster: prior to the summit, there was an attempt made on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to assassinate Valorum, while during the summit itself, the entire [[Trade Federation Directorate]], minus [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], were murdered in a plan orchestrated by Palpatine. The summit ended prematurely with nothing decided, and in the end the Senate enacted the taxation without allowing for the corporations to arm themselves against [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] raids.

Shortly after the end of the summit, Senator [[Orn Free Taa/Legends|Orn Free Taa]], leader of the Rim faction and member of the [[Allocations Committee|Allocations]] and [[Financial Appropriations Committee]]s, discovered that a large amount of [[Aurodium/Legends|aurodium]] stolen from the Trade Federation at Dorvalla by the Nebula Front had made its way into Valorum's bank account. This forced Bail Antilles, leader of Valorum's own Core faction and chairman of the [[Internal Activities Committee/Legends|Internal Activities Committee]], to charge Valorum with corruption and bring him before the [[Supreme Court/Legends|Supreme Court]]. This created a decisive shift in power in the Senate towards the Rim faction, which quickly passed measures prohibiting the Chancellor from using Jedi or the [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]] without first informing and gaining consent of the Senate. [[Mas Amedda/Legends|Mas Amedda]], a Senator of the Rim faction, was installed as [[Vice Chair/Legends|Vice Chancellor]] at this time, in an effort to block any further proposals that Valorum or his faction might make.

[[File:Amidalabeforesenate.jpg|thumb|[[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] just before calling for the [[Vote of No Confidence/Legends|Vote of No Confidence]] on Valorum's leadership.]]

While this was going on, Palpatine (in his [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] persona) had instructed the Trade Federation to arm themselves, and to [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|blockade]] Naboo&mdash;to protest both the taxation and as an act of revenge against Palpatine, the Senator who had proposed the trade summit that had been so disastrous to the Federation. Shortly before the blockade, Naboo's [[King/Legends|King]] [[Ars Veruna/Legends|Ars Veruna]] had abdicated and then been assassinated, and was replaced by the young [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], who due to her inexperience, had given Palpatine carte blanche in his Senate conduct. He urged Valorum to intervene, but the Trade Federation Senator, [[Lott Dod/Legends|Lott Dod]], was able to stall any procedures, making Valorum look weaker and weaker with every passing moment.

After being personally contacted by Queen Amidala, Valorum secretly approached the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] and illegally requested that they send [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] to Naboo as [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassadors]]. This resulted in a landing of Trade Federation forces on the planet; however, the Jedi, [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], were able to bring the Queen to Coruscant to address the Senate directly. Although she bore no ill will towards Valorum for his inaction, Palpatine informed her that he would take no further action and that, even though only a few months were left in his term, a new Chancellor would have to be elected immediately if Naboo were to be saved. The young Amidala deferred to Palpatine's greater experience, and upon addressing the Senate, called for a vote of no confidence in Valorum. It passed, and the election process began.

==Candidates==
{{Quote|Bail Antilles remains the front-runner. Ironically, the crisis at Naboo has drawn the Core Worlds into a tighter circle. Where Antilles has always been in danger of being dismissed as the candidate most likely to follow in Valorum's footsteps, he is suddenly the darling of those advocating for strong, central authority.|[[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]]|<ref name="Darth Plagueis (novel)">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>}}
[[File:SenatorBailAntilles.jpg|thumb|left|140px|[[Bail Antilles/Legends|Bail Antilles]], [[Core Faction/Legends|Core faction]] candidate.]]

As far back as Amedda's election to Vice Chair, Taa had decided on nominating Palpatine as the Rim faction's candidate, assuming that he could be counted on stopping Valorum's program of government interference. Despite stating what a surprise it was to be chosen, Palpatine had obviously been planning a run for the Chancery for some time; among the various elite of Galactic politics, the [[Galactic Corporate Policy League/Legends|Galactic Corporate Policy League]] had pledged to support him in a bid for the highest office. Palpatine must have seen even more attractive to him now, as in Palpatine's own words, the situation would give him a large sympathy vote. Additionally, as an independent, many saw him as a compromise candidate who would avoid the extremes of politics, while others viewed him as a naïve and inexperienced puppet who could be controlled. As Palpatine was known as advocating changing policies and imagery on government property that offended nonhumans, and for avoiding conflict, he presumably appealed to nonhumans and pacifists; and as a [[Human/Legends|Human]] Senator of a Human world that was being threatened by an aggressive nonhuman corporation, he presumably appealed to [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentrists]], and anti-corporate campaigners.

[[Ainlee Teem/Legends|Ainlee Teem]], a [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] [[Junior Representative/Legends|representative]] of [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]], was also nominated. Due to his homeworld, he was presumably nominated by a rogue group of Rim factioneers who did not like supporting someone that was not even in their own party. He received the backing of the [[Corporate Policy League]].

Finally, Bail Antilles, the Human Senator of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] was the third candidate. He was no doubt selected to represent the Core faction that he led.

==Election and aftermath==
The factors favored Palpatine, and the Senate voted overwhelmingly in favor of him. Although by the time he had taken office the Naboo situation had already been [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|resolved]], he promised to reunite the disaffected among the people and restore the remembered glories of the Republic. Although his efforts at reform would be stymied (by his own design), he would win his [[Supreme Chancellor election, 28 BBY|re-election]] in [[28 BBY/Legends|28 BBY]], only to be given an unlimited tenure via a [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|Constitutional]] amendment in [[24 BBY/Legends|24 BBY]] at the onset of the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]].

Shortly after losing the vote, Antilles retired from the Senate and was replaced by his relative-through-marriage, [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]]. The Core faction would become Palpatine's prime seat of power despite winning the election as the Rim faction nominee. The Rim faction would also lose a lot of influence due to this and eventually the Clone Wars where many of its senators and planets seceded to join the CIS.

Following his removal from office, Valorum retired from politics, and spent the last few years of his life writing an [[Holding Back the Tide|unsuccessful autobiography]] and doing work for the [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|Refugee Relief Movement]].
